newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to make radio address on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to make radio address on Thursday.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin will make a radio address to the nation on Thursday, a Kremlin spokesman said.
He said the speech would be broadcast at 11 a.m. (0700 GMT) on all main stations, but did not say what it would cover.

RIA news agency said on Wednesday that Yeltsin, 65, had chosen the radio for regular addresses because it is "the cheapest and most democratic mass medium which reaches even those corners of the country which are not covered by television".
Yeltsin all but disappeared from public view in late June, shortly before he was re-elected for a second term.
He has often looked stiff and moved and spoken slowly in television appearances since then. But he recently started holding more official meetings.

Yeltsin said on September 5 that he would have a heart operation and has been in hospital since September 13. Aides say he is working a maximum of three hours a day as he prepares for the heart bypass operation, due in six to 10 weeks time.
